1.explanation:
• ComboBox.js: core implementation must recognize the new readOnly prop, set the <input> to readOnly, suppress user interactions (e.g. typing or opening the menu), and apply a CSS class for styling.  
• index.js: must add readOnly to defaultProps and propTypes so the prop is documented and type-checked.  
• ComboBox.stories.js: needs a new story entry demonstrating the readOnly state with knobs/controls for playground and a default copy-and-paste example.  
• ComboBox-test.js & ComboBox-test.e2e.js: unit and integration tests must verify that when readOnly=true, the input has the attribute, the menu does not open on click/keyboard, and appropriate classNames are applied.  
• e2e/components/ComboBox/ComboBox-test.e2e.js: end-to-end coverage should confirm that read-only behavior persists in a real browser environment.  
• _combo-box.scss: styling must include rules scoped to the read-only CSS class (e.g. input[readonly] or .bx--combo-box--readonly) to gray-out text ($text-placeholder/$text-primary), disable pointer events on icons, and enforce the correct padding, border, and icon colors as shown in the design mocks.
1.bug_scenario: The provided mocks show a new read-only variant of the ComboBox component. In the first “no input” state, the field renders with placeholder text in $text-placeholder color, a transparent/dashed border, and disabled icons ($icon-disabled color), while maintaining the same 16px horizontal padding and 72px right-side spacing for the icon. In the “filled” state, the selected text appears in $text-primary, the bottom border is solid ($border-strong-01), and the clear and dropdown icons remain visible but styled as disabled. The component must still use the same spacing and layering as the enabled ComboBox, but the input itself should not be editable and should reflect the read-only styling.

2.explanation:
• ComboBox.js and index.js: need to add and export the readOnly prop, pass it down to the input and suppress dropdown toggling when readOnly is true.
• ComboBox.stories.js: update the Storybook playground to include a readOnly control and create a default “readOnly” story for copy/paste.
• ComboBox-test.js and ComboBox-test.e2e.js: add unit and end-to-end tests that verify the readOnly attribute is applied, input is non-editable, icons do not open the menu, and the proper CSS class is rendered.
• ListBoxField.js: the ComboBox’s input field is rendered here; it must accept readOnly, forward it to the <input> element, and apply a new read-only CSS class (e.g. “bx--list-box__field--readonly”).
• _combo-box.scss and _list-box.scss: add styles for the new read-only modifier class to implement the exact spacing, placeholder text color, disabled icon color, and border style as shown in the design artifacts.
2.bug_scenario: The user needs a new “readOnly” mode for the ComboBox component in the React package. When the readOnly prop is true, the text input portion of the combo box should not be editable or openable but should retain the same spacing, icon placement, and typography as the enabled state. Placeholder text and helper text should use the “secondary” and “placeholder” color tokens, the icons should use the “icon-disabled” color token, and the border should be the standard strong border color. The two provided design images show the exact horizontal spacing measurements (16px padding, 72px right padding to the icon in collapsed state, 8.5px between icons when an item is selected) and the text/icon color tokens for both “no input” and “filled” states.
